advisories.title: The two advisories are carried under unqualified ids ADV-1 / ADV-2, where every adopted decision in this run qualifies them by reviewer and generation
advisories.detail: Adopted practice is consistent: D-104 records CLAUDE-V11-A1 / CLAUDE-V11-A2 / CODEX-V11-A1; D-105 records 'CLAUDE-V8-A1 (ADV-V8-01: ...)', keeping both the qualified and the original id; D-108 records CLAUDE-V14-A1 / CODEX-V14-A1; D-111 records CLAUDE-V7-A-1. Most directly on point, D-107 faced this identical generic string - its Claude verdict also used 'ADV-1' - and the adopted entry reads 'Advisory CLAUDE-V2-A1 (/date roster) travels as honesty work.' D-112 instead carries bare ADV-1 / ADV-2. Once this lands in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md the log will hold D-107's ADV-1, renamed, and D-112's ADV-1, not renamed, denoting unrelated findings.
advisories.whyNotAFinding: The substantive requirement is met: the advisories are recorded and dispositioned, which is what CLAUDE-D110-S1 was about, and nothing false is stated. Resolution stays deterministic because the same table row pins the Claude verdict digest, the draft attributes them as 'Claude advisories', and Codex carries zero advisories this cycle, so no two findings can be conflated. Id qualification is a convention that guards against collision, and there is no live collision to guard against here. Denying CONSENT over it would be enforcing a house style rather than correcting an error, which is not what the SHOULD-FIX bar is for.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: On a successor or at adoption, prefer the D-105 form - a qualified id with the original in parentheses, for example CLAUDE-V3-A1 (ADV-1) and CLAUDE-V3-A2 (ADV-2) - so the decisions log stays unambiguous without losing the link back to the frozen verdict's own ids.
